title: Fruit and shoot borer of Okra

Header: Fruit and shoot borer of Okra
Earias vitella (Fabricius) (Lepidoptera Noctuidae); E. insulana (Boisduval) (Lepidoptera Noctuidae) luddi, sundi

Prevention: Remove and destroy affected fruits and shoots; for shoots by nipping them off below pest hole.
Grow carrot, sunflower and buckwheat to attract pest away from okra.
Cover beds with polythene sheet 45 gauge (0.45 mm) thickness for three weeks before sowing, this will reduce the pest in the soil.
Use pheromone traps (5-8 per acre), put at least one foot above the crop canopy.
Monitoring: Look for withered and drooping terminal shoots, shedding of buds and flowers, bore holes in fruits and deformed fruits.
Look for blue eggs on the underside of leaves and brown, boat shaped larvae in terminal shoots and fruits.
Set up pheromone traps (3-5 per acre).
If 2-4 silvery green adults are caught per trap then consider direct control actions.
Direct Control: Trichogramma chilonis at a rate of 40,000 per acre.
Apply neem cake at 100 kg/acre at the time of transplanting.
Spray azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) as neem oil at a rate of 1000-2000 ml in 200-400 litres of water per acre.
Apply azadirachtin 5% w/w neem extract concentrate at 80 ml in 160 litres of water per acre
Conserve predators of the borer, such as coccinellids, parasitic wasps, dragonflies, spiders, robber flies, reduviid bugs, praying mantis, fire ants, earwings and ground beetles.
Restrictions: Use personnel protection equipments (PPE) while using chemical pesticides
